summary: recce/services/rdp.py is intentionally minimal: one X.224 Connection Request PDU, parses the RDP Negotiation Response/Failure ([MS-RDPBCGR] 2.2.1.2), and emits two findings — rdp_no_nla (Standard RDP accepted) and rdp_fingerprint. That is roughly nmap's rdp-enum-encryption stage 1 and nothing else. Everything past the security-negotiation PDU — Basic Settings Exchange (MCS Connect Initial/GCC), TLS/CredSSP layer, NTLMSSP inside CredSSP, active BlueKeep channel probe, server encryption level, restricted-admin flag, TLS cert data — is entirely absent. The module also produces zero cross-service facts: hostname, DNS domain, OS build, and NetBIOS name are trivially extractable from the CredSSP/NTLMSSP CHALLENGE_MESSAGE and would seed known_users/hostnames/domains/relay_targets for SMB, LDAP, and Kerberos scanners, but nothing is emitted today. BlueKeep is named in the finding text but never actively probed. No credentialed path (spray/validate) exists despite creds being passed to analyze().

missing_capabilities.name: rdp_ntlm_info_extraction
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: [MS-RDPBCGR] 5.4.5 Enhanced Security; [MS-CSSP] 3.1.5; [MS-NLMP] 2.2.1.2 CHALLENGE_MESSAGE (TargetInfo AV_PAIRs: MsvAvNbComputerName, MsvAvNbDomainName, MsvAvDnsComputerName, MsvAvDnsDomainName, MsvAvDnsTreeName, MsvAvTargetName; Version field = OS major/minor/build)
missing_capabilities.description: After selecting CredSSP/Hybrid, complete TLS then send NTLMSSP NEGOTIATE_MESSAGE inside the CredSSP TSRequest.negoTokens. The server's CHALLENGE_MESSAGE leaks NetBIOS hostname, NetBIOS domain, DNS FQDN, DNS domain, DNS forest, and OS build (e.g. 10.0.19041). This is what nmap rdp-ntlm-info does and it is the single highest-ROI RDP recon primitive. Currently zero of this is captured.

missing_capabilities.name: bluekeep_active_probe_cve_2019_0708
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: [MS-RDPBCGR] 2.2.1.8 Client MCS Channel Join Request; MS_T120 static virtual channel (name 'MS_T120', channel id 0x1F). PoC by @zerosum0x0 / metasploit auxiliary/scanner/rdp/cve_2019_0708_bluekeep.
missing_capabilities.description: Module NAMES BlueKeep in the rdp_no_nla finding but never probes it. Real detection: complete X.224 + MCS Connect Initial with a client-mcs-channel-def that includes MS_T120 in Client Network Data, join it twice, and infer patched/vulnerable from the disconnect provider ultimatum PDU (unpatched sends 0x00000005 on second join; patched drops or returns different code). Delivers a definitive CVE-2019-0708 verdict instead of a candidate-by-banner guess.

missing_capabilities.name: tls_certificate_extraction
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: [MS-RDPBCGR] 5.4.5.1 TLS Security; RFC 5246. Same primitive already used by the ssl scanner.
missing_capabilities.description: When SSL/CredSSP is negotiated, wrap the socket with ssl.SSLContext (verify_mode=NONE) and pull peer cert: subject CN, SANs, issuer, notBefore/notAfter, key size, signature alg, self-signed. Feeds hostnames and domains cross-service, and produces the standard weak-cert findings (self-signed default 'WMSvc-*', expired, sha1WithRSA, RSA<2048). None of this is done today.

missing_capabilities.name: credentialed_nla_spray_validate
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: [MS-CSSP] 3.1.5 TSRequest exchange with SPNEGO/NTLM authInfo; xfreerdp /u /p /d supports validation via NLA.
missing_capabilities.description: analyze() accepts creds but ignores them. A one-shot NLA authenticate — either via socket-level NTLMSSP AUTHENTICATE_MESSAGE inside CredSSP or by shelling xfreerdp with a 0-sec grace timeout — yields authoritative valid-creds proof AND detects Restricted Admin acceptance (pass-the-hash surface). Compare with rdesktop-style RC4 fallback probing for Standard RDP servers.

missing_capabilities.name: mcs_connect_initial_server_data_parse
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: [MS-RDPBCGR] 2.2.1.4 (Server MCS Connect Response), 2.2.1.4.2 Server Core Data (rdpVersion, clientRequestedProtocols, earlyCapabilityFlags), 2.2.1.4.3 Server Security Data (encryptionMethod, encryptionLevel, serverRandom, serverCertificate — Proprietary RSA cert w/ RC4 key or X.509)
missing_capabilities.description: After X.224 selects Standard RDP, send Client MCS Connect Initial + GCC ConferenceCreateRequest with Client Core/Security/Network Data blocks. Parse Server Core Data for RDP version (0x00080005 = RDP 8.1, 0x00080004 = RDP 8.0 etc.) and Server Security Data for encryption level (NONE=0, LOW=1, CLIENT_COMPATIBLE=2, HIGH=3, FIPS=4) and encryption method (40/56/128-bit RC4 or FIPS). LOW/40-bit are CWE-327 findings; also gives exact server version for BlueKeep/DejaBlue confidence.

missing_capabilities.name: rdp_neg_req_flags_restricted_admin_probe
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: [MS-RDPBCGR] 2.2.1.1.1 RDP Negotiation Request negReqFlags: 0x01 RESTRICTED_ADMIN_MODE_REQUIRED, 0x02 REDIRECTED_AUTHENTICATION_MODE_REQUIRED, 0x08 CORRELATION_INFO_PRESENT.
missing_capabilities.description: Current _X224_CR hardcodes flags=0x00. Sending 0x01 (RESTRICTED_ADMIN) or 0x02 (REDIRECTED_AUTH) and observing whether the server accepts the negotiation vs. returns a NEG_FAILURE reveals whether Restricted Admin / Remote Credential Guard is enabled — Restricted Admin allows pass-the-hash and is a direct lateral-movement enabler once you get NT hashes from another module.

missing_capabilities.name: credssp_version_cve_2018_0886
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: [MS-CSSP] 2.2.1 TSRequest.version field (value 2 = pre-patch, 3 = March-2018 CredSSP RCE patch, 4/5/6 = later); CVE-2018-0886.
missing_capabilities.description: The TSRequest that CredSSP wraps around NTLM carries a version integer. A server that still negotiates version <= 2 is missing the CVE-2018-0886 patch and is vulnerable to the CredSSP logon-cred injection RCE. Requires wrapping TLS + issuing a minimal TSRequest and reading back the version — same connection you'd use for rdp_ntlm_info.

missing_capabilities.name: dejablue_version_gating
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: CVE-2019-1181 / CVE-2019-1182 / CVE-2019-1222 / CVE-2019-1226 — RDS pre-auth RCE affecting Win7 SP1 through Server 2019 pre-Aug-2019.
missing_capabilities.description: Once OS build is extracted via rdp_ntlm_info, gate a DejaBlue-candidate finding on build < August-2019 patch levels (10.0.17763.720, 10.0.17134.984, 10.0.16299.1358, 10.0.15063.2021, 10.0.14393.3181, 6.1.7601.24499). Wins the confidence-vs-noise fight because it uses observed build rather than banner.

missing_capabilities.name: tls_cipher_and_protocol_enumeration
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 8446/5246; RDP TLS is an unmodified TLS stream after X.224 selects SSL.
missing_capabilities.description: Enumerate offered TLS versions (SSLv3/TLS1.0/1.1 acceptance) and cipher suites (RC4, 3DES, NULL, EXPORT, CBC-only) once inside the TLS wrap. Same primitives as ssl_scan; RDP TLS is a common holdout of TLS1.0 and RC4 on older Windows RDS.

missing_capabilities.name: rdp_udp_transport_detection
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: [MS-RDPEUDP] 3389/UDP with SYN datagram (0x01 flag) — reveals Reliable/Lossy UDP transport support.
missing_capabilities.description: Purely 3389/tcp today. UDP transport is an alternate fastpath channel and its presence hints at RDS 8.1+ deployments. Low value but trivial once a UDP-capable probe framework exists.

missing_capabilities.name: rd_gateway_bluegate_cve_2020_0609
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: CVE-2020-0609/0610 — Remote Desktop Gateway UDP handshake bug on 3391/UDP.
missing_capabilities.description: Not on 3389 but a natural sibling scan when RDP appears — probe 3391/udp for RDG DTLS handshake and version gate. Module today ignores RDG entirely.

missing_capabilities.name: smartcard_redir_and_rd_channels_enum
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: [MS-RDPBCGR] 2.2.1.3.4 Client Network Data — server echoes accepted static channels in Server Network Data 2.2.1.4.4; virtual channel names hint at feature set (rdpsnd, drdynvc, cliprdr, rdpdr).
missing_capabilities.description: Cheap enumeration of which RDP virtual channels a server accepts (clipboard, drive, printer, smartcard) — informational, but useful for post-exploitation planning.

cross_service_wire_gaps: hostnames: NetBIOS + DNS computer name from NTLMSSP CHALLENGE_MESSAGE AV_PAIRs (MsvAvNbComputerName, MsvAvDnsComputerName) — never emitted; would feed SMB, LDAP, Kerberos scanners and cred_quickconnect
domains: DNS domain + forest tree from NTLMSSP CHALLENGE_MESSAGE (MsvAvDnsDomainName, MsvAvDnsTreeName) — never emitted; would seed Kerberos realm and LDAP baseDN discovery
hostnames: TLS certificate subject CN + SAN when SSL/CredSSP negotiated — never captured

relay_targets: NLA-off servers (Standard RDP accepted) are cleartext-cred receivers of on-path attacks; a Restricted-Admin-enabled server is a PtH relay target — neither is emitted as a relay_targets fact
os_fingerprint: NTLMSSP Version field yields exact OS major.minor.build (e.g. 10.0.17763) — never emitted; today's rdp_bluekeep_candidate has to guess from nmap banner
known_users: none directly, but a valid-cred find from NLA spray would seed known_users with (user, domain) — module ignores creds entirely

hashes: NLA/CredSSP NTLMSSP exchange technically produces an NTLMv2 challenge/response pair on the wire during authenticated probes; if we ever perform NLA cred validation, capturing our own outbound response is moot but a MITM/relay-mode probe (relay recce) could stash server challenges — currently unimplemented
priority_gaps: rdp_ntlm_info_extraction — one TLS wrap + one CredSSP TSRequest + parse NTLMSSP CHALLENGE_MESSAGE AV_PAIRs. Yields hostname, DNS domain, forest, and exact OS build. Feeds hostnames/domains/os across the whole fabric. Highest ROI by a wide margin.

bluekeep_active_probe_cve_2019_0708 — MS_T120 channel-join probe turns the current name-only 'candidate' finding into a real CONFIRMED CVE-2019-0708 verdict; matches metasploit auxiliary scanner behavior.

tls_certificate_extraction — reuse existing ssl-scan cert parsing to pull CN/SAN/self-signed/expiry/keysize once CredSSP or SSL is negotiated; seeds hostnames cross-service and yields the standard weak-cert findings.

credentialed_nla_spray_validate + restricted_admin negReqFlag probe — analyze() already receives creds and ignores them; adding NLA validation gives valid-cred proof and (via negReqFlags=0x01) tells us whether Restricted Admin is on, which is the RDP-PtH lateral movement gate.
notes: Module is 217 lines and does essentially one PDU. All post-negotiation intelligence ([MS-RDPBCGR] MCS Connect, [MS-CSSP] TSRequest, [MS-NLMP] AV_PAIRs, TLS layer) is unimplemented. BlueKeep is verbally referenced in the rdp_no_nla finding text but never actively probed — this is the single most misleading current behavior because it reads as a check but is not. There is no credentialed code path despite the analyze() signature accepting creds. There is no emission into the cross-service known_users/hostnames/domains/relay_targets pipeline even though CredSSP/NTLMSSP would trivially yield hostname, DNS domain, forest, and OS build.
